name: Gold 200
description: The everyday consumer favourite — warm, slightly saturated colour with a nostalgic golden cast. Forgiving in most daylight conditions, a safe first roll for anyone new to film.

name: ColorPlus 200
description: Kodak's most affordable colour negative film. Softer contrast and muted saturation compared to Gold 200 — a gentle, vintage-leaning look.

name: Ultramax 400
description: A versatile mid-speed colour film that handles overcast days and indoor light better than the 200-speed stocks, without losing Kodak's signature warmth.

name: Monopan 50
description: A slow, fine-grain panchromatic black & white film with a wide tonal range. Best in bright daylight or on a tripod — reward for the extra care is exceptional sharpness.

name: Phoenix 200
description: Ilford's experimental colour negative stock — expect halation, colour shifts, and visible grain. Loved by shooters who want a distinct, imperfect look rather than accuracy.

name: Fujicolor 200
description: Cooler and more neutral than Kodak's consumer stocks, with gentle greens and flattering skin tones. A dependable everyday roll.

name: Fujicolor 400
description: A punchier, more saturated step up from Fujicolor 200, with enough speed for indoor and lower-light shooting while staying sharp.

name: T800
description: A fast colour negative stock built for dim conditions — evenings, indoors, overcast days. Leans warm and richly saturated, with noticeably more grain than the 200/400-speed rolls in exchange for the extra stops of light.

name: Color 200
tagline: A classic Chinese film brand's comeback
description: Lucky Film's first new colour negative stock in over a decade — a brand-new C-41 formulation, not a reissue of the old stock. ISO 200, 36 exposures, priced to be an easy everyday roll while the brand rebuilds its reputation from scratch.

name: QuickSnap 27exp
description: A single-use camera loaded and ready to shoot — built-in flash, fixed focus. Fuji's 400-speed colour stock leans cooler and more neutral than Kodak's, with true-to-life greens and punchy but not overblown saturation. No settings to think about, just point and shoot until the roll runs out, then bring the whole camera in for developing.

name: FunSaver 27exp
description: Kodak's single-use film camera, pre-loaded with high-speed colour film for reliable shots indoors and in low light. Expect warm, saturated tones and noticeably more grain than the 200/400-speed rolls — part of the charm under flash. Simple flash button, no focusing needed.

name: EC35
tagline: Reusable 35mm camera, includes a free Ultramax 400 24exp roll
description: A beginner-friendly reusable 35mm point-and-shoot with a built-in flash and a 25mm f/10 optical-grade acrylic lens. Slide the front cover open to shoot, closed to lock the shutter — no settings to fuss over. Runs on 1x AA battery (not included). Comes bundled with a free roll of Kodak Ultramax 400, 24exp, to get you shooting right away.
about: The KODAK EC35 is a beginner-friendly point-and-shoot camera that strips away the complexity of film photography, putting the pure joy back into every frame. Featuring a tactile slide cover for instant protection and a built-in flash, it's designed to be tossed in your bag and ready for every golden moment — pocket size, colour surprise.

features.title: Slide cover
features.text: Keeps your lens completely safe while doubling as an automatic shutter lock to prevent accidental shots when closed.

features.title: Built-in flash
features.text: Optimised for versatile shooting environments — remember to advance your film to activate the shutter and flash.

features.title: 25mm lens
features.text: A wide-angle lens ideal for street photography and portraits.
